scopeLimits: Research was limited to anonymous public first-party discovery and bounded GET/POST endpoint inspection.
No login, credentials, private token, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare/WAF bypass, or unsafe landholder/owner/address/contact/titleholder/tax/account fields were requested or retained.

One diagnostic curl used a narrow TLS certificate-validation exception while checking the two official geodata service hosts; no global TLS disable was used. This was not used to authenticate or bypass access controls.
No exact-point parcel query was attempted because no public parcel endpoint was identified; this is not evidence of citywide absence.
No GeoJSON sample was retained because no safe native parcel identity plus full polygon was publicly verified.
uncertainty: DCCFE/OTR is evidenced as the official custodian, with specific regional Kara conservation evidence, but no anonymous parcel-level publication was verified.
The Geodata portal's public application and protected GeoServer host indicate a national geospatial platform, but do not by themselves prove cadastral coverage or a usable parcel API for Kara.
A WAF block, authentication response, or lack of a public viewer is not evidence that Kara lacks cadastral coverage.
runtimeReadiness remains held pending independent serial qualification of a real adapter and safe public parcel geometry.
